Actually, waiting tables is a good place to start because one of the biggest part of sales is an ability to get along amicably with all kinds of people. That doesn't come naturally for everybody - it takes practice.

Sales, ultimately, is about meeting needs. People have needs, and if you can meet those needs they will gladly purchase your product or service. You need to be meeting the right people, with the right product - but you also need the personality and communication skill that will allow you to communicate that you do indeed have the answer they are looking for.

When you are waiting tables, you are also actually selling. The people have a need, they are hungry. You bring a menu, that has products you are offering to meet that need, if they see something they like, they order it. The rest is about actually delivering that product, and dealing with any problems that crop up, whatever those problems might be. If the food is good, and the service is pleasing, that usually also generates a tip.

So the question becomes what do you like - I always say you should sell a product or service you actually believe in - people are really good at detecting insincerity. That is never a problem if you actually like the product. Then your conversation will have the ring of truth to it - and it is a hell of a lot easier to sell something when you are honest about it.
